chunks: As for this narration of Saad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: 'Ja'far ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal narrated to us from Ula' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he mentioned the hadith.'
Except that he said: 'And each of the two shall give charity every day with two mudds of food.'
So it does not contradict the earlier narrations, because this narration can be understood as a type of recommendation (mustahabb), while the earlier ones are understood as obligatory (fard/wajib).
ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile differing narrations on the amount of charity for expiation of fasting?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between narrations by distinguishing between obligatory (wajib) and recommended (mustahabb) expiations for the elderly who break their fast. He interprets the specific fixed amounts in earlier reports as mandatory duties, while viewing the daily charity of two mudds in this specific chain as a voluntary act of piety, thereby harmonizing the legal rulings within the Shia tradition.
